data.content: Plan (complexity: high, contained to the compaction contract and tests): 1. Base an isolated codex/knots-075e-protected-v2 worktree on refreshed origin/main and carry tasks/approval-ledger.md, tasks/lessons.md, and the Wave 1 checklist into the branch. 2. Replace the generation-two manifest with a deny-unknown-fields protocol-v2 schema rooted only under .knots/v2: immutable generation/control paths; distinct canonical control, immutable archive, and credential-scoped inbox refs; registered writer heads; snapshot descriptors; lossless raw packs; and exact event-id/content-hash entries. Validate IDs, hashes, paths, ref roles, uniqueness, predecessor epochs, acknowledged writer dominance, and an explicit provider-protection marker. 3. Replace direct generation publication with an immutable-object-first activation request model: publish archive and pack objects create-only, then advance the protected control ref by exact expected-head CAS. Model rollback as a higher control epoch selecting an archived predecessor while preserving all raw packs and generations. Direct publication fails closed unless a validated provider marker binds the canonical/control/archive/inbox refs and writer identity. 4. Disable generation-two local deletion: the replication fence validates the protected-v2 marker/control contract but never removes legacy paths, packs, archives, or objects. Preserve legacy .knots/events, .knots/index, and .knots/snapshots as non-authoritative compatibility data. 5. Add focused Rust tests for schema completeness and rejection, pack/index losslessness, ref/path isolation, marker fail-closed behavior, immutable-first/CAS ordering, monotonic rollback, and retention. Add a checked-in fixture/provenance document generated by released v0.17.6 and an integration test proving its legacy-path commit cannot change canonical .knots/v2 tree hashes. 6. Run cargo test compaction, the v0.17.6 compatibility fixture, make install-hooks, and make sanity. Commit with Sneka attribution, push to GitHub, open the normal PR, wait for CI, merge, verify exact origin/main SHA, then advance the Knot to SHIPPED. Risks: schema shape must remain small enough for later provider/local-cache leaves; provider enforcement is intentionally represented and validated but not activated live in Wave 1; no archive/raw-pack/history deletion and no provider mutation are in scope.
